task: Check whether TypeSolver::unify leaves a reusable solver unchanged after contradictory nested constraints.
observation: The standalone Map[T,T] versus Map[Int,String] probe returned false but left T resolving to Int. A rollback trail now restores partial bindings, union parents, path compression, and requirement joins on failure.
impact: A caller that reuses the solver after a failed constraint could observe stale inference state. The caller audit found Moss checker paths generally terminate or discard that solve; the demonstrated issue is the TypeSolver operation contract, with no source-level wrong acceptance established.
evidence: g++ -std=c++17 -O0 -Isrc tests/tooling/check_type_solver_atomicity.cpp -o tmp/check_type_solver_atomicity && tmp/check_type_solver_atomicity (baseline failed at the unresolved-T assertion; fixed version passes)
src/type_ir.hpp: TypeSolver::unify, bind, resolve, and root

resolution.summary: TypeSolver::unify now rolls back its mutation trail when any nested constraint fails; focused recovery and state-preservation assertions pass.
